title: Docking and molecular dynamic simulations of Mithramycin-A and Tolfenamic acid against Sp1 and survivin.
authors: Lambring, Christoffer Briggs; Fiadjoe, Hope; Behera, Santosh Kumar; Basha, Riyaz
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子对接和MD模拟研究药物Mithramycin-A和Tolfenamic acid与转录因子Sp1及survivin的结合，虽聚焦药物-蛋白互作而非TF-DNA结合，但涉及TF靶向和分子模拟方法，对TF-DNA互作建模有参考价值。
abstract: Therapeutic targeting of Sp1 transcription factor and survivin, are studied in various cancers due to their consistent overexpression. These markers result in poorer cancer prognoses and their downregulation has been investigated as an effective treatment approach. Mithramycin-A and Tolfenamic acid are two drugs with innate anti-cancer properties and are suggested to be able to target Sp1 through GC/GT DNA binding interference, however in-depth binding and mechanistic studies are lacking. Through docking analysis, we investigated Mithramycin-A and Tolfenamic acid in terms of their specific binding interactions with Sp1 and survivin. Through further molecular dynamics simulations including Root Mean Square (RMS) Fluctuation and RMS Deviation, rGYr, and H-bond analysis, we identified critical residues involved in drug interactions with each protein in question. We show Mithramycin-A as the superior binding candidate to each protein and found that it exhibited stronger binding with Sp1, and then survivin. Subsequent molecular dynamics simulations followed the same trend as initial binding energy calculations and showed crucial amino acids involved in each Mithramycin-A-protein complex. Our findings warrant further investigation into Mithramycin-A and its specific interaction with Sp1 and their downstream targets giving a better understanding of Mithramycin-A and its potential as an effective cancer treatment.
abstract_zh: Sp1转录因子和survivin的靶向治疗因其在多种癌症中的持续过表达而受到研究。这些标志物导致较差的癌症预后，其下调已被研究作为一种有效的治疗方法。Mithramycin-A和Tolfenamic acid是两种具有天然抗癌特性的药物，并被认为能够通过干扰GC/GT DNA结合来靶向Sp1，然而缺乏深入的结合和机制研究。通过对接分析，我们研究了Mithramycin-A和Tolfenamic acid与Sp1和survivin的特异性结合相互作用。通过进一步的分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟，包括均方根 (Root Mean Square) 波动和均方根偏差、rGYr以及氢键分析，我们识别了与每种目标蛋白药物相互作用中的关键残基。我们显示Mithramycin-A是与每种蛋白结合的最佳候选药物，并发现其与Sp1的结合更强，其次是survivin。随后的分子动力学模拟遵循了初始结合能计算的相同趋势，并显示了每个Mithramycin-A-蛋白复合物中涉及的关键氨基酸。我们的发现值得进一步研究Mithramycin-A及其与Sp1及其下游靶标的特异性相互作用，从而更好地理解Mithramycin-A及其作为有效癌症治疗方法的潜力。
